node.title: DLI primitive Haar-event correlation identity
node.statement: Let t=2^m and draw a uniform binary vector on the cyclic domain of size n. For each dyadic junction j<m, let O_j be the event that its integer Haar-skew band vanishes in the odd moment frequencies U_j, and let T_m be the terminal level-m one-moment null event. Then the original t-null event is exactly T_m intersect intersection_j O_j; P(O_j)=B_j/2^n and P(T_m)=Z_m/2^n. If Prim deletes the antipodally invariant vectors, P(Prim intersect T_m intersect all O_j)=(Z_0-C_1)/2^n. Therefore J_prim=P(Prim intersect T_m intersect all O_j)/(P(T_m) product_j P(O_j))=2^(nm)(Z_0-C_1)/(Z_m product_j B_j). In particular J_prim<=sqrt(2n) is exactly a constants-bearing discrete-Haar multi-event correlation inequality.
node.attack_surface: Check the cyclic quotient indexing, odd-frequency sets, integer rather than mod-two Haar skews, Vandermonde weights, terminal alphabet, first-owner deletion, and the number m+1 of marginal events in the normalization.
node.falsifier: A binary vector for which the recursive Haar events disagree with the original first t moments, a junction marginal whose binary-cube probability is not B_j/2^n, or a primitive correlation ratio differing from the telescoping formula.
node.notes: This preserves all cross-depth cancellation in one probability ratio. It proves no upper bound on that ratio and does not establish positive or negative association of the Haar events.
